diagrams.title: **The blueprint for every agent in this course
diagrams.caption: **The blueprint for every agent in this course.** Your app sits in the middle. It thinks by calling a model, acts by calling tools, and talks to people through a UI.
diagrams.svg:

diagrams.title: **Six stages of agentic systems
diagrams.caption: **Six stages of agentic systems.** Read the red arrow first: as systems get more capable, testing them, securing them, putting guardrails around them and being able to see what they are doing all become harder, and more important. Tap any stage to explore it.

diagrams.title: **Stage 1 is a straight line
diagrams.caption: **Stage 1 is a straight line.** No lookups, no tools, no memory beyond the current conversation.

diagrams.title: **Fixed pipe vs decision-maker
diagrams.caption: **Fixed pipe vs decision-maker.** Traditional RAG always retrieves, even when retrieval can't help. Agentic RAG picks the right source for each question, and can loop until it has what it needs.

diagrams.title: **Three pillars around the brain
diagrams.caption: **Three pillars around the brain.** Retrieval tells the LLM where to find information, tools let it act, and memory lets it keep track of what has happened so far.

diagrams.title: **The key visual difference
diagrams.caption: **The key visual difference: one has an end, the other doesn't.** An agentic workflow is a task with a finish line. An autonomous agent is a loop that keeps watching, acting and learning, which is exactly why it needs the strongest guardrails.

diagrams.title: **A newsroom made of agents
diagrams.caption: **A newsroom made of agents.** Each agent is good at one thing, and the messages between them (violet) are where the coordination happens. Those messages are what agent protocols, coming next, standardise.
